Two-factor authentication (2FA) is a security system that requires users to provide two different authentication methods to access a service. This adds an additional layer of security by requiring both a user's username and password as well as a second form of authentication, such as a code sent to their phone or generated by an authentication app.

Here is an example of how two-factor authentication works:

1. The user logs into their account on a website or application.
2. The system asks the user to provide a username and password.
3. The system generates a one-time password (OTP) and sends it to the user's phone via SMS or through an authentication app.
4. The user enters the OTP into the system to complete the login process.
5. The system verifies the OTP and grants access to the user's account.

Two-factor authentication provides an extra layer of security by requiring both something the user knows (their password) and something they have (their phone or authentication app). This makes it much more difficult for hackers to gain access to a user's account, as they would need both the username and password as well as the OTP to gain access.

Two-factor authentication is commonly used by banks, online retailers, and other services to protect sensitive information and prevent unauthorized access. It is an important security measure that can help protect users from identity theft and other types of cybercrime.

2 cups of all-purpose flour
